title: Cleveland family says they've reported dog attacks for months, fear another
text:
A Cleveland family says they’re living in fear after what they describe as two violent attacks by the same neighbor’s dog, one in September 2024 and another last Friday, June 19. They say they’ve reported the incidents repeatedly, but the dog is still next door.
CLEVELAND, Ohio -A Cleveland family says they’re living in fear after what they describe as two violent attacks by the same neighbor’s dog, one in September 2024 and another last Friday, June 19.
They say they’ve reported the incidents repeatedly, but the dog is still next door. In their backyard on highland road, the family says something as simple as letting their dogs outside has turned into a “safety drill. ” They say they now take their pets out one at a time and keep bear spray close by.
“I lost my shoes, my glasses, my phone, everything was in the yard. I had nothing. ” Brandi Proctor said. Nick Proctor, who is Brandi’s son says the repeated incidents have taken a serious toll on the family, emotionally and financially.
“It has been just a complete nightmare,” Nick Proctor said. “We have had over $10,000 in emergency vet bills and hospital bills. My dad was hospitalized. Both dogs were hospitalized.
It has been the worst thing that could ever happen. We are not asking for any type of monetary compensation. We don’t have a GoFundMe. All I’m asking for and seeking is justice.
”The Proctors say the first attack happened in September 2024, when the neighbor’s dog got loose and attacked their 12-year-old dog, Bella, and bit their father. Amber Proctor said her father had let Bella out after work when the neighbor’s dog came through a chain-link fence.
“So, my dad came home to his dog, Bella, who’s 12, after work and let her out per usual and they were outside a minute or two and this dog came through the chain link fence, that is the neighbor’s fence, grabbed her by the throat, ripped her under into their yard, where my dad had to throw himself over the fence to struggle with the dog to try to get Bella free. The dog bit him,” Amber Proctor said.
Second attack: dog allegedly gets loose again The family says it happened again last week, when the dog got loose and ran into their backyard while their mother was outside with three dogs; Bella, Charlie and Rollie.
“So I was standing here talking to Annette for a minute. The other two dogs were deeper in the grass and Rollie let out a little bark and I looked down and he had looked out the driveway, and I looked and I said, what’s wrong, Ro? And he turned his head and he started to run,” she said.
“And no sooner did he start to run, that dog come around the corner here at the edge of the house and ran after him, grabbed a hold of him from behind and he was screaming. ” Rollie, who the family says weighs about 25 pounds, was rushed to an emergency vet. The family says he is still alive but recovering with stitches and multiple drainage tubes.
“The other two dogs were deeper in the grass and Rollie let out a little bark and I looked down and he had looked out the driveway, and I looked and I said, what’s wrong, Ro? And he turned his head and he started to run and no sooner did he start to run, that dog come around the corner here at the edge of the house and grabbed, ran after him, grabbed a hold of him from behind and started and he was screaming,” she said.
The Proctors say they’ve filed police reports and contacted animal control, and they’re now asking the city to intervene before another incident occurs.
“I feel like my family, our animals have not been helped the way that we should have been by animal control, by the Cleveland police,” Amber Proctor said. “They tell us to call and report, but when we call, it seems like we’re a nuisance. So, it’s a lose-lose situation, and it’s really unfortunate. So, all I want to see is this dog just taken before it harms somebody else.
”“How many times do you have to deal with this until something happens? We’ve made phone calls to Cleveland Police. We’ve made phone calls to the prosecutors, animal wardens, CPS, everybody, and nothing’s happening,” Nick Proctor added. The family says they plan to bring their concerns directly to their council representative during a community meeting at their local library Wednesday night.19 News has reached out to the landlord of the renters next-door who own the dog.
